scope: Cooperative initialization competition and retry after pre-publication process termination

finding.before: Initializer was outside workspace lock, so a competing init could create the requested workspace while another initializer was paused before publication.
finding.after: Initialization holds the same sibling lock through staging construction/publication, rechecks target inside lock, and rejects existing workspace.

validation.red_regression: Isolated unlocked initializer copy allowed competing init exit0 instead of workspace_busy exit4.
real_cli: Paused initializer prevents competing init from publishing
Killed pre-publication initializer releases lock and new init succeeds
Existing workspace duplicate init rejected with unchanged bytes
validation.fixture_corrections: Resolved macOS /var vs /private path alias for barrier; fixture-owned idle sidecar removed before unsafe-lock probes; child pipes closed on all paths.

limits: Killed initializer staging retained; retry builds a new staging, not recovery of the old one.
No protection claim for external writers bypassing the lock protocol.
Lifecycle remains PARTIAL: other transaction/cleanup boundaries, Windows, network filesystem and power-loss durability unverified.
No live provider, app, commit, push or release.
